chapter: The Vitaphone film and studio work
title: Who played in the studio bands and the standard tunes
summary: The regular band with Gene Wright was topped up with transient players, and everyone knew about fifty old tunes such as Back to Alabama.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Who were some of the musicians that you took with you to the studios?
Oh, I...they...we had our regular band--Gene Wright and the one's that's on that picture.nearly and, of course, there's a lot of them that I can't remember their names that would

probably be in town for a couple of weeks, and they'd come in and say, 'I'm a saxophone player,' and we couldn't give...we take your name and address. If we need a saxophone player, we'd call him. You know. And then some of 'em hung around for a year or two, and then they'd be gone. You couldn't find them. You'd get a job and couldn't look for them, you have to take somebody else, you know. As I told you, there were maybe fifty old tunes that everybody knows--'Back to Alabama' and 'Georgia Brown' and all that stuff--all the musicians know it, and when we go out on a job, you carry...you play half of the night and just play them old tunes that everybody knew. See?
